lines.text: Pay up.
Paid in full.
Cha-ching.
Next!
Exact change.
Keep the change.
Sold!
No refunds.
Streak! Tip jar's full!
Cash rain!
Count 'em!
Jackpot!
Compound interest!
Don't stop, don't stop!
Interest due!
Collected!
Feel that?
That's the fee!
Read the fine print!
Smash and grab!
Overdue!
Home run! Pay up!
Out of the park!
Gone! No refund!
Grand slam!
Returned to sender!
Ow! That's extra!
Hey! Watch the leather!
You'll pay for that!
Ow. Charging you.
Rude!
Bruised my billfold!
Hands off!
That's going on your tab!
Here we go. Pay up.
Line up, bots.
Open for business.
Cash only!
Round two. Bring cash.
Come on, then!
Step up, pay up.
Ready to collect.
Level up! Raise!
Profit!
Upgrade me. I'm good for it.
Bonus time!
Now we're rich.
Treasure! Mine!
Open it! Open it!
Finders keepers!
Slice! Hold on!
I'm coming!
Not on my tab!
Nobody collects her!
Big bill. Big payday.
Good. Bigger tip.
Gold! Mine!
Shiny. Mine.
That one pays double.
Pay up, bots.
They'll feel it.
I know. Pay up!
Nobody touches her.
Still mine to guard.
Coins. Bolts. Mine.
You good, Slice?
Bolts are wages. Collect.
Walls cost. Worth it.
That's a tip. I keep tips.
They want her circle. Not on my watch.
Plates cost more. Pay up.
You're bleeding, Slice.
I'm covering you. Tab's open.
Nobody touches her. Nobody.
Something big's coming. I can smell the invoice.
Then I'm reading mine. Pay up.
Holding, Slice?
Twenty-five waves. I'm owed a bonus.
Last stretch. Pay up.
Then it carries my bill.
Overtime pays double.
A door number. Does it come with a door?
And the bolts they drop?
And the plates? The big ones?
And then?
Bolts. Somebody's paying me.
By the guy with the stamp.
Cleared things. Somebody's hat. Somebody's clock. That could be me.
Cover me, Slice. I'm collecting a refund.
Does existing come with a receipt?
Door's down. Still no sender.
Every bot that's come at us. They're coming from down there.
Every page turned over. DENIED.
Evidence. Every bill has a paper trail.
Feed's broken. Their pay is mine now.
Flat. Every one. Pay up.
Guard Slice. Swing at anything chirpy. Pay up.
Hello? Sender? I'd like a word, and a receipt.
I am.
I've seen it. I don't need to be told.
It's filed. All of it.
It's got my notice in there somewhere. I keep receipts.
It's not signed.
It's watching the circle.
It waited for me to take it. Three times. Refused all three.
Last of the Crew. Then the big one. Exact change.
Leased. By you.
Locks have keys. Keys have owners. Owners get paid.
Meaning?
My stamp. My door.
Neither do I. Pay up.
Nerve's free. The swing's extra.
Next time I'm billing the Floor.
No.
Nobody signs it. That's the whole trick.
None of this is mine. I'm keeping it anyway.
Not for free.
Nothing. Not even a doormat. I'd say that's rude, but I'm the one with no address.
Nothing's free.
One lever. No sign. Somebody trusts the floor.
One notice, returned. Where's my tip?
Open up. I know you're in there. It's a stamp, not a person.
Overhead. Don't look at me like that.
Pages four and five are the small print. Nobody reads the small print. I do.
Read what?
Received. In full. Pay up.
Refused.
Refused. I can do refused. Free of charge.
Refused the paper three times. Put that in writing.
Return to sender.
Return to sender. Which sender? I want a refund.
Signed by nobody. Told you.
Since when?
So does my refund. Pay up.
So the order is only a form.
So we exist.
Spiders. Bigger than anything so far, and not bigger Yo Bots.
Stamped out. So they're the Department's. Employees.
STRIKE. THIS. ADDRESS. Sounds worse when it's yours.
"Strike this address." Stamped DENIED. Ha.
Struck from the record.
Take it.
That's my stamp. Torn.
The notice is in my pocket. Evidence.
The order's a form. A form can be answered.
Then give it one. You've got the stamp.
Then I'll make it a refund.
Then I'll read it the invoice.
Then I've been collecting what's owed. Good. Now I want the lever.
Then it can be denied.
Then it can read me the bill.
Then let's file it. Pay up.
Then they're out of walls. Let's file it. Pay up.
Then we answer it. Pay up.
There's a door. Doors have senders.
They keep coming down the same path. Nobody's lost. They know the address.
They keep the order here. Every copy of it.
They're all the same unit.
They're not bigger Yo Bots. They're deliveries.
They were only ever stamped out. Nobody asked them.
Those bolts are the same ones they've been paying me.
Two out of the yard. That's a tip.
Two. Put me next to you.
Under time. Charge extra.
Void. I don't take bills I didn't order.
Void your own stamp.
Waiting's billable.
Wallit. One wallet, one bat, no refunds. They stamped me "Return to sender" and threw me in here.
Wasn't going to. Not for free.
Where do I sign for this bat?
All those forms. Blank now.
And you?
Anything. Yourself.
Belt's quiet. I miss the noise. Cheap.
Dead letters. Nobody's coming for these.
Finders keepers. Quietly.
Foreman said "not finished." Neither am I.
Forty. Forty-one. Somebody short-changed me.
I'm standing here, aren't I. Exact change says yes.
In case somebody needed you.
Is that a mailbox or a bad loan?
It's filed. I can stand here free.
Item one: wallet, leather. That's me. Where's my cut?
Last time this notice went in my ledger. This time I read the whole thing first.
Nine stones. Looks like padding on the bill.
Number on the wall. Mine?
One door, in my hand. One stamp. I'll try it again.
One door in my name. I still hear it close.
One notice down. Billing it.
Pages read, doors filed. Last time I read along. Louder this time.
Quiet is cheap.
Receipt. Proof I was here.
Registrar read slow. I read faster.
Slice. Straight answer. Who stamped me?
Slow is never cheaper. Ask my bill.
Somebody at the Server's desk kept my name. Mine only.
Sounds bad for business.
Standing in your ring. Rent's due.
Take it. I'll bill the Department.
Tap. Tap. Hear that? Hollow. Like a bank at closing.
The gate stamped me back. Interest owed.
The Server's paper is already pinned in the hub. Refused, in full.
The Server still holds out its paper.
Then I'll start the tab. Pay up, eventually.
Then you're due a head.
Three refusals. Clean ones.
Two doors. Heavier bill, bigger crew. Keep up.
What did it ring for?
Who pays you for it?
You held the ring while I was out.
You're not afraid of the circle?
You've got no head. How do you hear?
You were in the hub.
Zero delivered. Six returned. Somebody's cooking the ledger.
Always. Don't thank me.
Behind you.
Blank is a fresh account.
Clean. Stand as long as you like.
Closer.
Counted. Four would be rude.
Door's yours. Stay clear of the lamp.
Every slip on the wall was pinned. The Floor sends fewer now.
Fine. Keep swinging.
Good. Keep swinging.
I'm armed.
Last time you signed for the notice. Two names, one pen. Do it again.
Let it. Ring is full.
Look west. The trail. Lost things, lying where they landed.
Out. North-east.
Paid. In kind. Stay.
Quiet is rent. Take it.
Sender unknown. Billing void.
Take them.
The door never shut. It will stay open.
The Hollow knows our door. Somebody will knock.
The Registrar reads one name aloud. Last time it was yours alone.
The Server kept two names last time. It will ask for two.
They can't hear you.
Two doors. Wallit's is next to mine. Knock on it.
Two numbers, side by side. Same pen. Same line.
Wallit.
You did. Don't boast.
You filed the ledger alone. The Foreman reads it back differently now.
Yours. Keep the receipt.
A gummed label on Brim's hook reads BRIM, in Brim's own slow hand.
Brim hangs on the wall by the door number, band on, left of the desk. It has an address.
Chime rings once for the right address. It is the quietest bell in the Hollow.
Spare chirps once, properly, and the Hollow answers.
Spare is in the doorway of the ring, lid on straight, cheering at nothing in particular.
Tick is wound. Nobody had to be the Department to do it.
Tick keeps the hour. Every pin where it should be.
Twelve slips on the office wall, every one pinned. The Department files itself.
Lids on! The door opens for us this time!
The ledger knows us! Uploading... a door!
Second notice! This address is still unknown.
Special delivery! Notice of striking!
Tick. Notice delivered on the hour, as written. Slice stood. Good hour.
Tock. The gate stamped you back. Doors keep time too. Yours is still open.
Slow belt, red lamp. Someone's hour was stopped there. Mine nearly was.
Three refusals. I counted each one. A paper refused thrice is still a paper. Mind it.
The order has no signature. Nobody was ever keeping its time. Strange, to know that.
It's late and it's filed. The hour's yours now, Wallit. Spend it.
Nobody has wound me since the Department stopped. I keep the hour out of habit.
Nobody. That is the habit.
The belt had a clock too. It ran slow on purpose. Slow is cheaper.
Then you and the foreman disagree. I side with the bill.
Blank forms, all of them. That is a quiet kind of hour. Nobody owes anything in it.
It sounds like rest. I would like some. Is that allowed?
Did you ever have a head? I had one once. I miss the weight.
A postmark, half yours, torn. Half a name is a better start than I had.
Hats on that belt. Dozens. I looked for mine. I didn't look away.
The spiders bow, did you see? Politely. I'd tip my brim, if I could tip.
DENIED. Good stamp. The forms went blank, and blank is a fresh start.
Filed. I have an address now: Brim, the circle, left of the desk. Grand.
The gate rang when you came back. A hat knows a door when it hears one.
Through the brim, Wallit. Everything arrives through the brim.
Three refusals on the Long Walk. I counted them from here.
Hats go where heads go, Wallit. In spirit. I had your head in mind.
The pages went blank and I felt lighter. I think I was a form once. A form for a head.
I would settle for a wall. A wall with a hook. An address, Wallit.
Hello! Uploading victory! I am... mostly uploading! Chirp!
Hello! Plated Alpha, stamped INVALID! Sorry! I was told to cheer!
Hello! Hooks! I know hooks! I was on one! Not finished, now free!
Chirp! Spiders en route! En route to... I have no route. I live here!
Hello! Every page the same! I read them all! Wallit read faster! Chirp!
Hello! Filed! Uploading... nothing! I'm just here! Chirp chirp!
Chirp! I was half a Yo Bot on a hook. Now I am half a Yo Bot in a nice room!
Slice looked at me. Then she looked away. That is a welcome! Chirp!
They called me a spare. Kept in case. Chirp... in case of what?
Somebody does?
It's filed! The order is gone! What do I cheer for now?
Uploading... me! Chirp! ...Oh. That one worked.
Ding. Notice returned, tip owed. I've a thing that wants fetching.
Ding. The gate. I heard it ring from here. Another errand, if you'll carry it.
Ding. The belt carried a bell like me once. Fetch this and I'll pay.
Ding. Three refusals, and I rang for each. One more errand. It pays.
Ding. Blank forms. Everyone lost something in those. Fetch one back.
Ding. Filed. Last errand. It pays in full, as the books go.
Ding. I ring when a thing is lost. It rang all through your chapter.
Everything. Ding. It is a loud room, the world.
Ding. The server's bell was mine once. A cousin. It rang for papers.
I ring for what is missing. Ding. Which is better, I think.
Ding. All six chapters, all six things back. The room is quieter now.
Quiet is cheap, and I rang for it anyway. Ding. Thank you, Wallit.
